item.title: Complete Electrode Model
item.description: The Complete Electrode Model (CEM) is the standard forward model for real EIT measurements (see Electrode Models).

item.title: Current Patterns
item.description: A current pattern is a boundary current g with \int_{\partial\Omega} g\,\mathrm ds = 0 (or electrode currents with \sum_\ell I_\ell = 0).

item.title: Dirichlet Problem
item.description: In the Dirichlet problem the voltage on the boundary is prescribed.

item.title: Dirichlet-to-Neumann Map

item.title: Electrode Models
item.description: The mathematical boundary conditions have to model how current actually enters the body through L metal electrodes e_1,\dots,e_L\subset\partial\Omega.

item.title: Forward Map
item.description: The forward map of EIT takes a conductivity to the boundary operator it generates: \mathcal F:\ \gamma \mapsto \Lambda_\gamma \quad(\text{or } \gamma\mapsto\mathcal R_\gamma = \Lambda_\gamma^{-1}).

item.title: Neumann Problem
item.description: In the Neumann problem the current density on the boundary is prescribed.

item.title: Neumann-to-Dirichlet Map
item.description: Real EIT devices inject currents and measure voltages.

item.title: Point Electrode Model
item.description: The point electrode model idealises every electrode as a single boundary point x_\ell\in\partial\Omega (see Electrode Models).
